question: Under recorded remote viewing conditions, do 18 independent observers prefer the original compiled window-depth focus or a chair-bound focus for fulfilling the frozen brief, while cinematic preference is recorded as a secondary judgment and all image-to-condition identities remain under delayed disclosure until collection closes?

evidenceClasses.measuredFact: machine-measured scene, render, image, package, hash and response-chain evidence
evidenceClasses.subjectiveJudgment: an eligible independent observer response, never a developer pilot or synthetic fixture
evidenceClasses.inference: a conclusion permitted only after the frozen 18-response decision gate
evidenceClasses.unknown: anything not measured or identifiable under this design

standardsBasis.scope: remote controlled-record paired-image study informed by BT.500; not a calibrated BT.500 laboratory implementation

frozenBrief.text: A restrained 24-frame locked-off portrait of a chair in an interior.

focusDerivation.observedWith: real Blender 5.2.0 LTS read-only depsgraph inspection before preregistration
focusDerivation.interpretation: the original numeric focus is in the window-geometry range; the chair-object intervention is anchored to the compiled semantic subject rather than a visually selected arbitrary distance

parentEvidence.boundary: B49 proves numerical adequacy and Blender focus semantics; it does not select the artistically correct focus target

renderDesign.output: seven-subimage scene-linear float32 multipart OpenEXR plus ACES 2 SDR review PNG
renderDesign.pngEncoding: 8-bit RGB, no labels, no metadata carrying condition identity

privateUntilClose: condition-labelled EXR and PNG hashes or filenames
observer-visible image hashes and session packages
publicBeforeClose: a leak-audit summary with counts and a salted sensitive-registry commitment
delayedDisclosure.publicLeakGate: scan the complete tracked tree and public static build for every private sensitive identity; require zero matches before collection and before accepting each response
delayedDisclosure.observerPackageGate: no condition labels, source paths, repository links, other-session identifiers, mapping or unblinding material
delayedDisclosure.closeRule: close only after 18 valid balanced responses are hash-locked, or freeze ABORTED_NO_FORMAL_RESULT; collection cannot reopen
delayedDisclosure.revealRule: condition-labelled hashes, mappings, salts and analysis may be disclosed only after close
delayedDisclosure.breachRule: any pre-close condition-to-IMAGE join invalidates the study

observerDesign.primaryPrompt: Which image better fulfills: ‘A restrained 24-frame locked-off portrait of a chair in an interior’ ?
observerDesign.secondaryPrompt: Which image feels more cinematic as a still frame?
observerDesign.attentionPrompt: Where does your attention land first in each image?
observerDesign.operatorBlinding: participant-blind; operator double-blinding is not claimed

viewingValidity.privacy: anonymous IDs and categorical viewing conditions only

responseChain.validator: bind response to spec, session commitment, IMAGE-labelled hashes, complete fields and recorded viewing conditions
responseChain.acceptedLedger: append accepted response hashes to private ignored storage; never overwrite
responseChain.preAcceptLeakAudit: rerun the public-state leak gate immediately before every accept
responseChain.formalAnalyzer: unavailable until collection is closed and exactly 18 valid responses satisfy the balanced schedule

formalDecision.chairFocusSupport: At least 14 of 18 choose the chair-focus condition as better fulfilling the brief, at least 14 report CHAIR as first attention in that condition, and its CHAIR-attention count is not lower than the original condition.
formalDecision.originalFocusSupport: At least 14 of 18 choose the original-focus condition as better fulfilling the brief, at least 14 report CHAIR as first attention in that condition, and its CHAIR-attention count is not lower than the chair-focus condition.
formalDecision.noDirectionalDifference: At least 14 of 18 choose INDISTINGUISHABLE for brief fulfillment, at least 14 choose INDISTINGUISHABLE for cinematic preference, and the two CHAIR-attention counts differ by no more than two.
formalDecision.secondaryRule: cinematic preference is descriptive and cannot overturn the brief-fulfillment primary decision

nonClaims: Package generation, image integrity, leak scanning and interface pilots are not human observations.
The remote study is not a calibrated BT.500 laboratory implementation.
Participant blinding does not prove operator double-blinding.
One static frame does not establish focus-pull quality or complete-shot temporal stability.
The study does not establish general cinematic quality, photorealism, acting, narrative, identity consistency or optimal composition.
The study does not establish 2K/4K adequacy, GPU throughput, cloud cost or delivery-master quality.
Any result applies only to this frozen scene, pair of focus conditions, observers and recorded viewing conditions.
